# Skales

> Websites & systems for service businesses. Builds websites, online booking and follow-up automation for UK service businesses (trades and local operators). Run by Tom Griffiths, one person, in the United Kingdom.

Key facts:
- Builds websites, online booking and follow-up automation for UK service businesses (trades and local operators).
- One person: the person you message is the person who builds it.
- Twelve websites and one system run live on the site as working demonstrations; every business in them is fictional.
- One system a week is built in public on Instagram.
- Clients own their domain, code and accounts from day one; nothing is rented back to them monthly.
- Every build is hand-coded, with no page builder and no theme.
- Contact: thomasrgriffiths08@gmail.com · Instagram @tomxsystems (https://www.instagram.com/tomxsystems/)
- Book a call: https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/book/

## The builds
- [Atelier Voss](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/atelier-voss/): website for an invented architecture practice: A studio site with no photographs at all.
- [Cadence](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/cadence/): website for an invented field-ops software: The page is an operations board that never stops running.
- [MARÉE — Sel Obscur](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/maree/): website for an invented fragrance house: Ink through water, and a page that darkens as you descend.
- [SIGNAL 2027](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/signal/): website for an invented music & light festival: Type that reacts to how hard you scroll.
- [Long Exposure](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/long-exposure/): website for an invented long exposure: A film company's site that plays like a film you can scrub.
- [Overhead](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/overhead/): website for an invented overhead: Scroll to climb, and the valley draws itself in contours as you rise.
- [Southpaw](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/southpaw/): website for an invented boxing club, leeds: A boxing club site built as a fight card, run by a round timer.
- [Marrow & Pin](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/marrow-and-pin/): website for an invented tattoo studio, bristol: A flash wall that inks itself as you scroll past each sheet.
- [Hale & Partners](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/hale-and-partners/): website for an invented chartered accountants, harrogate: A year-end that settles, and the deadlines counted from today.
- [Fern Physio](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/fern-physio/): website for an invented fern physio: A drawn body with ten tappable points, and a booking flow behind it.
- [Kestrel Electrical](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/kestrel-electrical/): website for an invented two-van electrical firm: An electrician's page built as a fuse board: every job is a breaker.
- [Kerb & Camber](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/kerb-and-camber/): website for an invented kerb & camber mot centre: A UK number plate you type into, and the MOT date that comes back.
- [The system](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/system/): part of the system, shown for six invented businesses: One screen: every call caught, every job booked, and what still needs you.
- [Inbox and missed calls](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/inbox/): part of the system, shown for six invented businesses: Every call, text and form in one list. Missed calls get a text back in seconds.
- [Booking and the diary](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/booking/): part of the system, shown for six invented businesses: Customers book a real free time and pay a deposit. It lands in the right diary.
- [Quotes that chase themselves](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/quotes/): part of the system, shown for six invented businesses: Quotes from your price list that chase themselves until the customer answers.
- [Google reviews](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/reviews/): part of the system, shown for six invented businesses: Every finished job asks for a review. Replies take one tap.
- [Reminders that rebook](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/reminders/): part of the system, shown for six invented businesses: Yearly services, MOTs and regular cuts remind the customer and book themselves.
- [Results and ads](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/results/): part of the system, shown for six invented businesses: Where every job came from, what it was worth, and what the ads cost per job.

## Frequently asked
- **Do I actually own the website?** Yes. With Skales the domain, the code and the hosting sit in your own accounts from day one. It is set up so you could walk away tomorrow and lose nothing; that is the whole point.
- **Is there a monthly fee to keep my site online?** No. Skales does not charge a monthly platform fee to keep your own website alive. You pay for hosting and your domain directly, in your own name, at cost. If any quote you get includes a monthly fee to keep your own site online, that is rent.
- **How long does a build take?** A website on its own takes days. A full system with booking and follow-up usually takes one to two weeks. You get a date with the quote, and you can watch it being built in public.
- **Are the builds on this site real clients?** No, and deliberately so. Every business, person, review and phone number in the demonstration builds is invented, so nothing on this site exposes anyone Skales works with. They are real working software, just for businesses that do not exist.
- **Who actually does the work?** Tom Griffiths. Skales is one person: there is no account manager and no handover to a junior. The person you message is the person who builds it.
- **What kind of businesses is this for?** UK service businesses whose work comes in by phone: plumbers, heating engineers, electricians, roofers, kitchen fitters, landscapers, cleaners, salons and similar trades and local operators.
- **What happens after I book a call or send the form?** Tom Griffiths looks at your website, your Google listing and what happens when someone tries to reach you, then messages you three things: what is leaking, what to fix first, and what it is worth in jobs. If you want it fixed, you get a flat quote. If not, you keep the list.
- **Do you use page-builders or templates?** No. Every build is hand-coded, with no page builder and no theme, so it does exactly what your business needs and nothing it does not.
